sections.skill: Tell the paying customer from the user and the decision-maker

questions.prompt: A school pays for a reading app that students use. Who is the paying customer?

choices.text: The students who use the app every day
The app's designers who built the screens
The parents who never see the bill

questions.intro: The CUSTOMER is the person or organization who pays. The USER is the person who uses the product or service. Sometimes they are the same; sometimes they are different. A parent pays for a child's piano lessons; the child is the user. A company pays for software its workers use. There may also be a DECISION-MAKER who chooses, like a manager who approves a purchase. To sell well, you must convince whoever pays and decides, while also making the product work for the user.
questions.feedback: The school pays, so it is the customer.

questions.prompt: For a child's soccer camp, whose money pays?
questions.intro: Ask two questions about any sale: "Whose money pays for it?" and "Who actually uses it?" For a child's soccer camp, a parent's money pays and the child uses it. For a coffee you buy for yourself, the same person pays and uses. For office chairs, the company pays and the workers sit in them. Write down both answers every time; they guide who you talk to and what you build.
questions.feedback: The parent pays.
